back: Team performance assessments: how well the team works, judged against the marks of high-performing teams.
Forming, storming, norming, performing, adjourning.
Members meet and learn about the project and their formal roles. Independent, not yet open.
The team tackles the work, technical decisions and the management approach. Without openness the climate turns counterproductive.
Members adjust their work habits to support the team and learn to trust one another.
A well-organized, interdependent unit that works through issues smoothly.

front: Three Tuckman facts beyond the stages
back: Teams can get stuck or regress; teams that worked together before may skip a stage; stage length depends on dynamics, size and leadership.
Adding, removing, merging or switching members. Teams then need time to re-establish agreements, roles and shared goals.
Providing a reason for someone to act. Teams are motivated by being empowered to take part in decisions and to work independently.
Conditions of work: company policies, salary, physical environment. Too little causes dissatisfaction; enough does not create satisfaction.
Content of the work: achievement, growth, advancement. Enough of them leads to satisfaction.
Autonomy (how, where, when), mastery (improve and excel), purpose (make a difference). Once pay is fair, these matter most.
Achievement (challenging, reasonable goals), power (more responsibility), affiliation (belonging to a team).
X: people work only for income; hands-on, top-down style. Y: people want to do good work; coaching style that encourages creativity.
Maslow: motivation by self-realization, values and a higher calling. Ouchi: a job for life, focused on employees' well-being.
Plan in Plan Resource Management; tailor to the person and culture; intangible rewards can beat money; recognize throughout, not only at the end.

front: Emotional intelligence as a team tool
back: Reduces tension and raises cooperation: identify sentiments, anticipate actions, acknowledge concerns, follow up on issues.
Inbound: self-awareness, self-management. Outbound: relationship management. Team EI also lowers staff turnover.
Performing well in culturally diverse, complex situations: recognizing that people express themselves differently, without stereotyping.
More communication planning: clear expectations, conflict protocols, inclusion in decisions, cultural understanding, shared credit.
Distributed: cross-functional teams in different locations. Dispersed: each member may work in a different place.
Coaching: helps a person solve a specific problem themselves by asking questions. Mentoring: long-term sharing of knowledge and experience.
A regular lessons learned workshop, at least every iteration, to improve process and product. Blame-free; a few improvements the team can finish.
